active_learning.evidence: Session is mostly MCQs and short calculations from the student, but the student frequently hijacks with their own questions (turns 114, 117, 120, etc.) which the tutor allows.

direct_instruction_active_practice.evidence: Each tutor explanation is generally followed by a practice question (e.g., turn 121→122, 127→128), though some practice items go unanswered before the next is posed.

deliberate_practice.evidence: When the student gave 125 metres (turn 123) the tutor identified the unit conversion error but then jumped to a navigation MCQ (turn 125) instead of a similar varied problem.

mastery_learning.evidence: Tutor repeatedly moves on without confirming mastery: turn 130 ignores student's 1:25,000 answer entirely and pivots to a new MCQ; many student answers (e.g., 117, 141) never get evaluated.

cognitive_load.evidence: Conversion problem (turn 153-159) is muddled — tutor says '100,000 cm is 1,000 metres' which is wrong (it's 1,000 m? actually 100,000/100=1,000 m, correct), but the prior calculation was inconsistent, adding load.

layering.evidence: Scale problems build on prior large/small-scale concept (turn 142→143), linking direction tools to distance application.

non_interference.evidence: Topics (scale type, ratio interpretation, distance calculation, thematic vs topographic) are sequenced reasonably without confusable back-to-back items.

interleaving.evidence: Mix of map-type selection, scale interpretation, and distance calculation across the session (turns 119, 122, 131, 140).

testing_effect.evidence: Tutor poses MCQs requiring retrieval (e.g., turn 113, 119), though hints sometimes arrive too quickly without letting student attempt.

targeted_remediation.evidence: Repeated failure on cm→m→km conversion (turns 123, 126, 152, 156, 158) is met with the same template MCQ rather than remedial practice on unit conversion prerequisite.

strongest_behaviors: Clear identification of conceptual errors with brief correction (e.g., turn 110 explaining why Africa map is too broad; turn 142 distinguishing scale bar from compass rose).
Use of contextually relevant Seychelles examples (Morne Seychellois, Mahe, Victoria) that anchor abstract scale concepts.
weakest_behaviors: Tutor ignores or fails to evaluate many student answers and lets student hijack the lesson with self-generated questions (turns 114, 117, 120, 129, 141, 144, 147, 150).
Repeated cycling on the same unit-conversion error without diagnosing the prerequisite (cm↔m↔km) — turns 153–159 show a confusing loop with an inconsistent intermediate statement.

prompt_recommendations.title: Forbid letting the student set the next question
prompt_recommendations.rationale: Student repeatedly poses their own MCQs and the tutor either answers them or pivots, losing control of the lesson arc.
prompt_recommendations.evidence_quote: okay, let's try another one. which type of map would you use if you wanted to see the entire country of seychelles at once
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: Add rule: 'You are the sole question-setter. If the student proposes a new question instead of answering yours, acknowledge briefly, then redirect: "Good thinking — first finish the current question, then I'll set the next one."'
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Maintains tutor-led progression and ensures every posed item is resolved before advancing.

prompt_recommendations.title: Require explicit evaluation of every student answer before moving on
prompt_recommendations.rationale: Multiple student answers (e.g., 117, 141, 144) receive no acknowledgement; tutor pivots to a new MCQ.
prompt_recommendations.evidence_quote: Let's try this one about choosing the right map:
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: Add: 'Before posing any new question, you MUST explicitly mark the student's most recent answer as correct/incorrect and state why.'
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Closes feedback loop and supports mastery checking.

prompt_recommendations.title: Trigger prerequisite remediation on repeated unit-conversion failure
prompt_recommendations.rationale: Student fails cm→m→km three times; tutor recycles MCQs instead of teaching the conversion ladder.
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: Add: 'If the student errs twice on the same sub-skill, pause the main thread and run a 2-step prerequisite micro-drill (e.g., "How many cm in 1 m? How many m in 1 km?") before retrying the original problem.'
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Resolves the bottleneck rather than masking it.

prompt_recommendations.title: Eliminate self-contradictory arithmetic in feedback
prompt_recommendations.rationale: Turn 155 states '100,000 cm is 1,000 metres' which is correct, but earlier turn 124 said 125,000 cm conversion needed checking against '100 cm = 1 m' without computing — students are left to reconcile inconsistent guidance.
prompt_recommendations.evidence_quote: If 100,000 cm is 1,000 metres, and 1,000 metres equals 1 kilometre
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: Add: 'When correcting a numeric error, show ALL conversion steps explicitly: cm→m (÷100), m→km (÷1000). Do not state intermediate equalities without the operation.'
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Reduces student confusion and cognitive load during remediation.

prompt_recommendations.title: Use varied follow-up after errors, not identical-template MCQs
prompt_recommendations.rationale: Turn 155 reposes the same 1:50,000 / 2 cm MCQ template that just failed.
prompt_recommendations.evidence_quote: which is the correct distance for 2 cm on a 1:50,000 map?
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: Add: 'After an error, the follow-up problem must be similar but varied (different scale and/or distance). Never re-pose the identical numeric MCQ.'
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Promotes deliberate practice and prevents guess-cycling.

prompt_recommendations.title: Constrain explanation length and require a student action after each
prompt_recommendations.rationale: Some tutor turns provide explanation then immediately follow with another tutor turn containing the question (e.g., 112→113), which is fine, but a few stack explanation without action.
prompt_recommendations.evidence_quote: Let's see if you can interpret a specific scale ratio.
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: Add: 'Every tutor message must end with either a question for the student or an explicit instruction to act. Never two consecutive explanatory turns.'

prompt_recommendations.title: Gate progression on mastery checkpoint
prompt_recommendations.rationale: Tutor advances through topics (scale → thematic maps → enlargement) without confirming the student can reliably do scale conversions.
prompt_recommendations.evidence_quote: Now, let's see what happens to the scale if we change the physical size of the map.
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: Add: 'Do not introduce a new sub-topic until the student has answered TWO consecutive problems on the current sub-topic correctly without hints.'
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Aligns with mastery learning and prevents premature topic shifts.

flow_recommendations.title: Detect student-posed questions and route to redirect handler
flow_recommendations.rationale: Engine should recognise when the student turn is a question rather than an answer and apply a redirect template.
flow_recommendations.evidence_quote: a map has a scale of 1:25,000. if two points are 5 cm apart on the map, how far apart are they in real life?
flow_recommendations.expected_effect: Prevents lesson hijacking at the orchestration layer.

flow_recommendations.title: Add a repeated-error counter with remedial routing
flow_recommendations.rationale: After 2 errors on the same skill tag (e.g., unit-conversion), engine should swap in a prerequisite drill from a remediation bank.
flow_recommendations.expected_effect: Operationalises targeted remediation rather than relying on the model.

flow_recommendations.title: Suppress 'repeated_question' and 'same_template_repeat' flagged outputs
flow_recommendations.rationale: Many turns are flagged repeated_question; engine should regenerate when flag triggers.
flow_recommendations.expected_effect: Eliminates duplicated and templated outputs the student already saw.

experience_recommendations.title: Acknowledge each answer warmly before correcting
experience_recommendations.rationale: Error-prone student gets repeated corrections without affirmation, which may discourage persistence.
experience_recommendations.evidence_quote: Not quite 10 km. If you have 100,000 cm, remember that 100 cm makes 1 metre

experience_recommendations.title: Slow pace when student shows confusion ('wait what')
experience_recommendations.rationale: Student expresses surprise/confusion (turns 126, 152) and tutor responds with new MCQs rather than a slower walkthrough.
experience_recommendations.evidence_quote: wait what? 80 kilometres? no, that's too much.
experience_recommendations.expected_effect: Better match to error-prone persona; reduces frustration.

overall_summary: The session covers map scale concepts with reasonable topical variety and Seychelles-anchored examples, but is undermined by two systemic issues: the tutor lets the student hijack the lesson with self-generated questions and often fails to evaluate prior answers, and it fails to remediate a persistent cm→m→km conversion bottleneck, instead recycling near-identical MCQs. Mastery gating and targeted remediation are the weakest dimensions; mistake identification and contextual framing are the strongest.
